It was reissued in book form by Éditions du Rocher in 2003 (ISBN 2-268-04592-7), and an archive was made public in 2007 by GEIPAN.
COMETA was registered under the French law of 1901 on 24 February 1999 and became dormant around 2006; the report itself was not widely circulated because of copyright restrictions.

edges.label: French private defence committee
edges.note: The report states its own legal status on its title page: 'COMETA, an association governed by the Law of July 1, 1901', the French statute for non-profit associations. Its foreword, by former CNES chairman Andre Lebeau, and the account by the former director of the Institut des Hautes Etudes de Defense Nationale place its formation in the IHEDN Auditors Association after General Denis Letty approached IHEDN in March 1995.

edges.label: IHEDN origin; delivered to the Prime Minister
edges.note: TIER 3. What the report establishes: General Norlain, then director of the IHEDN, writes that 'when General Letty visited me in March 1995 at my office at IHEDN to explain to me his project for creating a new fact-finding committee on UFOs, I assured him of my interest and referred him to the management of the IHEDN Auditors Association'. What it does not establish is the city. Paris appears nowhere in the report in connection with COMETA; the IHEDN sits at the Ecole militaire in Paris, but that is knowledge brought to the document rather than read from it. Nor does the report record delivery to the head of government - it says only that its authors believed 'sufficient questions of national interest are raised for the Chief of State and the Prime Minister to be provided with this information.'
